column2: Why? GPIO 39 is input-only and has no internal pull-up resistor, so we add 10 kΩ to 3.3 V. When not pressed the pin reads HIGH; when pressed, the pin connects to GND and reads LOW. For the finished robot, the button moves to breadboard 2 on floor 3 so it is easy to press, connected by two wires to columns 27 and 29 (lengths in Part 6).

Not yet The 6 mm button is only for testing: in Part 6 Step 3 it is removed, then plugged in again on breadboard 2 on floor 3. The bench GND wire (WAGO − to pin G) is also only for testing: on the robot the shared GND comes from the black wire of LM2596 #1 to the 30P board.
